title: A map of quasi-coherent modules bijective on an affine open cover is an isomorphism
statement: Let $Y$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], $\varphi:\mathcal F\to\mathcal G$ a morphism of $\mathcal O_Y$-modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] between quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_Y$-modules [pqf-def-coherent], and $Y=\bigcup_{a\in A}W_a$ a covering of $Y$ by affine open subschemes. If for every $a\in A$ the map of sections $\varphi_{W_a}:\mathcal F(W_a)\to\mathcal G(W_a)$ is bijective, then $\varphi$ is an isomorphism of $\mathcal O_Y$-modules.

source.place: Schemes, Lemma 01IA (schemes-lemma-quasi-coherent-affine) and Lemma 01IB (schemes-lemma-equivalence-quasi-coherent) on each W_a, with Sheaves, Lemma 04TN (sheaves-lemma-glue-maps) for the covering; used in the proof of Morphisms, Lemma 01SB ('this may be checked on the members of an affine covering')

proof.text: *Step 1 (transport to a spectrum).* Fix $a\in A$ and put $R_a=\mathcal O_Y(W_a)$. The open subscheme $W_a$ is affine [def-pc-scheme]: there are a commutative ring $B$ and an isomorphism of schemes $k:\operatorname{Spec}B\to W_a$; since $\Gamma(\operatorname{Spec}B,\mathcal O)=B$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum], $k^\sharp$ on global sections is a ring isomorphism $\rho:R_a\to B$, and composing $k$ with $\operatorname{Spec}\rho:\operatorname{Spec}B\to\operatorname{Spec}R_a$ inverted (an isomorphism, by functoriality of $\operatorname{Spec}$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum]) gives an isomorphism of schemes $h_a:X_a:=\operatorname{Spec}R_a\to W_a$ whose map on global sections $R_a=\mathcal O_Y(W_a)\to\Gamma(X_a,\mathcal O_{X_a})=R_a$ is the identity. Let $g_a:X_a\to Y$ be $h_a$ followed by the inclusion of $W_a$, an open immersion with image $W_a$. Restrict along $g_a$ as in [lem-weil-pbc-module-restriction-open-immersion-colimits]: $\mathcal F|_{X_a}$ and $\mathcal G|_{X_a}$ are $\mathcal O_{X_a}$-modules with $(\mathcal F|_{X_a})(U)=\mathcal F(g_a(U))$, quasi-coherent by clause (2) of that node, and $\varphi|_{X_a}$ is a morphism between them by clause (1), with components $(\varphi|_{X_a})_U=\varphi_{g_a(U)}$. On global sections, $\Gamma(X_a,\mathcal F|_{X_a})=\mathcal F(W_a)$ with $R_a$ acting through $g_a^\sharp$, which on global sections is the identity of $R_a$; so $\Gamma(X_a,\mathcal F|_{X_a})=\mathcal F(W_a)$ and $\Gamma(X_a,\mathcal G|_{X_a})=\mathcal G(W_a)$ as $R_a$-modules, and $u_a:=(\varphi|_{X_a})_{X_a}=\varphi_{W_a}$, an $R_a$-linear map which is bijective by hypothesis.

source.place: Schemes, Section 01I6 (section-quasi-coherent-affine) and Lemma 01IA (lemma-quasi-coherent-affine): a quasi-coherent module on an affine open is studied on Spec of its ring of sections

proof.text: *Step 2 ($\varphi|_{X_a}$ is an isomorphism).* Write $\mathcal F'=\mathcal F|_{X_a}$, $\mathcal G'=\mathcal G|_{X_a}$, $\alpha=\varphi|_{X_a}$, and let $\tau$, $M\mapsto\widetilde M$, $\varepsilon$ be as in [lem-weil-pbc-affine-tilde-gamma-adjunction] for $R=R_a$. The counit is natural: $\alpha\circ\varepsilon_{\mathcal F'}=\varepsilon_{\mathcal G'}\circ\widetilde{u_a}$ as maps $\widetilde{\mathcal F(W_a)}\to\mathcal G'$, because under the bijection $\beta\mapsto\beta_{X_a}\circ\tau_{X_a}$ of clause (1) (with $M=\mathcal F(W_a)$, target $\mathcal G'$) both sides go to $u_a$: $(\alpha\circ\varepsilon_{\mathcal F'})_{X_a}\circ\tau_{X_a}=\alpha_{X_a}\circ\mathrm{id}=u_a$ since $\varepsilon_{\mathcal F'}$ corresponds to $\mathrm{id}_{\mathcal F(W_a)}$, and $(\varepsilon_{\mathcal G'}\circ\widetilde{u_a})_{X_a}\circ\tau_{X_a}=(\varepsilon_{\mathcal G'})_{X_a}\circ\tau_{X_a}\circ u_a=u_a$ by $\widetilde{u_a}_{X_a}\circ\tau_{X_a}=\tau_{X_a}\circ u_a$ and since $\varepsilon_{\mathcal G'}$ corresponds to $\mathrm{id}_{\mathcal G(W_a)}$. By clause (3), $\varepsilon_{\mathcal F'}$ and $\varepsilon_{\mathcal G'}$ are isomorphisms ($\mathcal F',\mathcal G'$ are quasi-coherent by Step 1). The bijective $R_a$-linear $u_a$ has an $R_a$-linear inverse $u_a^{-1}$, and since $M\mapsto\widetilde M$ is a functor (clause (1)), $\widetilde{u_a^{-1}}$ is a two-sided inverse of $\widetilde{u_a}$. Hence $\alpha=\varepsilon_{\mathcal G'}\circ\widetilde{u_a}\circ\varepsilon_{\mathcal F'}^{-1}$ is an isomorphism of $\mathcal O_{X_a}$-modules, with inverse $\varepsilon_{\mathcal F'}\circ\widetilde{u_a^{-1}}\circ\varepsilon_{\mathcal G'}^{-1}$.

source.place: Schemes, Lemma 01IA (lemma-quasi-coherent-affine: a quasi-coherent module on Spec R is the tilde of its global sections) and Lemma 01IB (lemma-equivalence-quasi-coherent: tilde and global sections are quasi-inverse equivalences), with Lemma 01I7 (lemma-compare-constructions) for the adjunction

proof.text: *Step 3 (back to $W_a$).* The inverse $h_a^{-1}:W_a\to X_a$ is an isomorphism of schemes, in particular an open immersion, so restriction along it is a functor $\Mod(\mathcal O_{X_a})\to\Mod(\mathcal O_{W_a})$ [lem-weil-pbc-module-restriction-open-immersion-colimits] (1), and functors send isomorphisms to isomorphisms; thus $(\varphi|_{X_a})|_{W_a}$ is an isomorphism of $\mathcal O_{W_a}$-modules by Step 2. For an open $V\subseteq W_a$, $(\mathcal F|_{X_a})|_{W_a}(V)=\mathcal F(g_a(h_a^{-1}(V)))=\mathcal F(V)$, with $\mathcal O_{W_a}(V)=\mathcal O_Y(V)$ acting through the composite of $g_a^\sharp$ and $(h_a^{-1})^\sharp$, which is the structure map of the open immersion $g_a\circ h_a^{-1}$, the inclusion $W_a\subseteq Y$, i.e. the identity of $\mathcal O_Y(V)$; and the component of $(\varphi|_{X_a})|_{W_a}$ at $V$ is $\varphi_{g_a(h_a^{-1}V)}=\varphi_V$. So $(\varphi|_{X_a})|_{W_a}$ is the restriction $\varphi|_{W_a}:\mathcal F|_{W_a}\to\mathcal G|_{W_a}$ of $\varphi$ to the open $W_a$ in the sense of [lem-weil-pbc-sheaf-isomorphism-local-open-cover] ($V\mapsto\mathcal F(V)$, components $\varphi_V$), and $\varphi|_{W_a}$ is an isomorphism of $\mathcal O_{W_a}$-modules.

source.place: Schemes, Lemma 01IB (lemma-equivalence-quasi-coherent), applied on the affine open W_a; transport along the isomorphism Spec R_a = W_a written by the agent

proof.text: *Step 4 (glue).* By Step 3, $\varphi|_{W_a}$ is an isomorphism of $\mathcal O_{W_a}$-modules for every $a\in A$, and $Y=\bigcup_aW_a$ is an open covering. By the 'if' direction of [lem-weil-pbc-sheaf-isomorphism-local-open-cover] (with $X=Y$, $\mathcal O_X=\mathcal O_Y$, $U_a=W_a$, $\alpha=\varphi$, $\mathcal M=\mathcal F$, $\mathcal N=\mathcal G$), $\varphi$ is an isomorphism of $\mathcal O_Y$-modules.
